actions.action: Spray the plant with 70% isopropyl rubbing alcohol, undiluted or diluted with water, repeating every 3-5 days for about 3-4 weeks
Test-spray alcohol on one leaf and wait 24 hours before a full spray
Buy a new bottle of 70% isopropyl alcohol without glycerin if yours contains glycerin
Manually remove scale with an alcohol-soaked cotton swab, then spray the spot and underside
Apply food-grade diatomaceous earth as an alternative
Spray a water, rubbing alcohol and dish soap mix and use a small paint brush to reach crevices
Rinse the plant with clean water after the alcohol spray
Dry the plant and clear the rosettes with a compressed-air duster
Keep the treated plant out of the sun until it has healed
Inspect new plants and spray them with alcohol before repotting

verdict.reason: The answer is a thread dump about killing soft-bodied pests with rubbing alcohol: it implies a pest problem without naming whiteflies, its main advice of alcohol spraying matches the fix that worked, and nothing it suggests is likely to harm the plant.
